\[
P(\text{Blue} | \text{Witness says Blue}) = \frac{P(\text{Witness says Blue} | \text{Blue}) \cdot P(\text{Blue})}{P(\text{Witness says Blue})}
\]

Substituting values:
\[
P(\text{Blue} | \text{Blue}) = 0.8, \quad P(\text{Blue}) = 0.2
\]
\[
P(\text{Witness says Blue}) = (0.8 \cdot 0.2) + (0.2 \cdot 0.8) = 0.32
\]
\[
P(\text{Blue} | \text{Blue}) = \frac{0.16}{0.32} = 0.5 \quad \text{(50%)}
\]

**If the witness is the taxi driver’s ex-spouse**, this could introduce bias. If the ex-spouse is more likely to lie (e.g., due to a motive), their accuracy decreases, lowering the probability the taxi was Blue. Conversely, if the ex-spouse is more credible, accuracy increases, raising the probability. Without specific data, the estimate changes qualitatively based on the ex-spouse’s reliability.
